top_strength: Two things were genuinely well done. First, she checked availability immediately and handled bad news cleanly — 'first let me just check availability, okay? One moment,' then told him Saturday was gone and offered Sunday, and he took it without friction. Leading with the date check before anything else is the right instinct. Second, her specialty-and-risk probe was thorough and better than most: she asked about walk distance and pushed for specificity ('Is it like a minute walk, half a minute walk?'), asked about access concerns at both locations including low-hanging trees, deep driveways and narrow hallways, asked about parking on the driveway versus the street, and ran a real high-value-item sweep covering safe, piano, large work equipment, washer/dryer, TV, artwork, marble and glass. She also confirmed disassembly and reassembly covers appliances when he asked about disconnecting the washer and dryer. And she closed the walkthrough live — created the link, texted it, and confirmed he received it before letting him go.
coaching_note: Roselyn, the single highest-leverage fix is the simplest one: get his name in the first fifteen seconds and use it. You went ten full minutes without ever addressing this customer as a person — 'Good afternoon, Einstein Moving, this is Roselyn, may I get your name?' and then 'Gonen, let me check that Saturday for you,' 'Gonen, I'm going to send you a link.' That one change lifts your politeness score and the whole feel of the call. Second, you promised pricing and then never delivered it or explained why. He asked whether packing dishes costs extra, you told him 'we'll walk you through how our pricing works,' and the next thing he heard was instructions to hang up. Close that loop out loud: 'The pricing depends on what we see, so we'll cover it live on the walkthrough — it takes about ten minutes and then I'll email you the full written estimate with no deposit required to book.' Third, you routed him to a walkthrough 'based on your home size' without ever asking the home size — ask for the origin square footage or bedroom count and the garage every time, because that's the number the routing decision rests on. Fourth, cut the dead air; you said 'one moment' or 'bear with me' six times, and it reads as unprepared even when you're just waiting on the system. Scope note on the score: this graded as a walkthrough_scheduler, so Pricing, Clock, Estimate and Save Your Ass were treated as out of scope and auto-granted their full 47 points per the N/A rule. That means the 66 is not comparable to a full sales call — on the 38 points this call was actually assessed against, you scored 19, so read this as a 50 percent call, not a 78 percent one.
phone_presence_notes: Polite words ('no worries,' 'take your time') on top of an almost entirely transactional, checklist-driven delivery — no name use at any point, no 'how are you,' roughly fifteen 'mm-hmm' acknowledgments in place of real responses, no acknowledgment of the one-week time pressure or the family paintings he volunteered, and six holds that stall the call's energy.
